transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in New York City, I'm Dwahili Sykowtow.
Large and violent anti-government protests took place across France today, with hundreds
of arrests.
Here's what it sounded like on the streets of Paris.
Police used batons, tear gas and water cannons to try and disperse more aggressive groups
of demonstrators.
Local media citing authorities said the vast majority of individuals marched peacefully.
The student-led protests began last month over claims of poor school infrastructure
and teacher absences.
President Emmanuel Macron pledged to go after individuals who committed crimes and damaged
property, saying there's no room for violence.
Meanwhile, the prime minister said there are limited funds to cover the damage caused by
protesters.
Higher fuel costs are putting pressure on the price of delivering groceries and holiday
purchases.
In Paris, Windsor-Johnson reports some products are more exposed to higher prices than others.
Even if your car runs on unleaded gasoline, diesel prices will hit you squarely in the
wallet.
Rutgers supply chain expert Rudolf Lucheiner says diesel powers the trucks delivering the
goods to store shelves.
"When you drive by a gas station, that's probably the number you should be looking at."
Refrigerated and frozen foods are under added pressure because deliveries can't wait.
And he says shoppers could pay more to get gifts delivered quickly.
"We've already seen FedEx add some additional surcharges to overnight deliveries.
I wouldn't be surprised if during the holiday season we'll see a little bit more of that."
He also says consumers may have a hard time separating fuel charges from the usual holiday
shipping fees.
Windsor-Johnson, NPR News.
In California, fire crews appear to be making progress as they try to contain a wildfire
south of Los Angeles.
The Norte Fire has burned at least 570 acres and is only 5 percent contained.
Steve Futterman reports already six homes have burned.
"Overnight, fire crews here made progress.
The Santa Ana winds have not gone away, but they are not nearly as strong as Friday.
That's good news for firefighters.
Steve Consialdi is a captain with the Orange County Fire Authority.
He says drones are helping to pinpoint dangerous areas.
"They can pinpoint where the hot spots are and they'll tell our firefighters where to
go there and we put water on it."
Officials say when the weather forecast earlier this week predicted strong winds, they pre-positioned
fire crews and equipment.
It paid off.
As soon as the Norte Fire broke out, they were able to quickly respond.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman in San Juan Capistrano, California.
The Henderson Fire near Camp Pendleton has burned more than 3,000 acres and that's only
35 percent contained.
You're listening to NPR News.
The Trump administration cancelled tens of millions in grants for teen pregnancy prevention
earlier this year, saying they normalize sexual activity for minors.
A new legal complaint alleges the administration then sent almost all of that money to a single
contractor through a secretive, rushed process, as NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin reports.
The complaint was filed by Hennepin County, Minnesota, one of the teen pregnancy prevention
grantees whose federal funding was cancelled earlier this year.
It alleges that the Department of Health and Human Services awarded $86 million to Guidehouse,
a private equity-backed consulting firm, and did so without the usual competitive process
local health departments and organizations have used for years.
Democracy Forward is representing the county.
Sky Parriman is the CEO.
Our focus is going to continue to be to use every legal tool we can to ensure the program
is administered as Congress intended.
The bid protest aims to block the award to Guidehouse.
The first hearing is scheduled for Tuesday in the U.S. Court of Federal Claims.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News, Washington.
The No Kings Coalition that began as anti-Trump rallies is refocusing their efforts on voter
turnout.
No Kings organizers with partner groups such as Black Voters Matter say more than 2,500
events are scheduled across the country, with their goal to bring out largest number of
midterm early voting numbers.
President Trump has long dismissed the No Kings events, calling them a joke.
He previously said, "I looked at the people, and they're not representative of this country."
I'm Dua Halisa Kautau, NPR News, in New York.
This message comes from NPR sponsor Charles Schwab.

topics.text: Large violent anti-government protests across France lead to hundreds of arrests
Higher diesel fuel costs pressure grocery and holiday shipping prices, Rutgers expert says
Norte Fire south of Los Angeles burns 570 acres, six homes lost, 5 percent contained
Henderson Fire near Camp Pendleton burns over 3,000 acres, 35 percent contained
HHS cancels teen pregnancy prevention grants, then awards $86 million to Guidehouse, complaint alleges
No Kings coalition refocuses on midterm voter turnout with over 2,500 events planned
